name: Iran nuclear programme
value: IAEA 13 Nov: no access; 440kg 60% HEU unverified
summary: IAEA report on 13 Nov says it cannot rule out diversion and does not know where Iran's Isfahan enrichment plant is
state: A confidential IAEA report circulated on 13 Nov says the agency does not know the exact location, safeguards status or contents of Iran's underground Isfahan enrichment plant, and has lacked continuity of knowledge over declared highly enriched uranium for more than a year (The National). It says the IAEA cannot confirm Iran has not diverted material; about 440 kg of 60% uranium is unaccounted for since June 2025 (AFP via Times of Israel). No new strike on a nuclear site, NPT withdrawal or evidence of weaponisation was found as of 15 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: There is no direct public health risk outside the region. Restricted inspections and 60% enriched stockpiles tend to raise the chance of diplomatic confrontation and further military action; travellers should follow FCDO travel advice for Iran.
rubric_hit: Watch: inspector access curtailed and ≥60% enriched stock unverified (IAEA, 13 Nov)

sources.title: The National — IAEA expresses concern over Iranian underground uranium-enrichment plant
Times of Israel — UN agency can't confirm Iran hasn't diverted nuclear material from peaceful activity, report says

why: A nuclear-armed Iran — or strikes to prevent one — could ignite the Gulf and send oil far higher.
drivers: Enrichment levels, IAEA access, Israeli/US military posture, snapback sanctions, talks.

rubric.alert: Strikes on nuclear sites, NPT withdrawal, or evidence of weaponisation.
rubric.watch: Enrichment at ≥ 60% or inspector access curtailed, or credible strike threats.
rubric.normal: IAEA access and active diplomacy; no escalation.
